faqs.question: Who should take this SOC Analyst course?
faqs.answer: This is for anyone who wants a real, hands-on entry into the world of security monitoring — including graduates of our Cybersecurity Foundations course, IT professionals looking to move into a SOC role, and anyone who enjoys the idea of watching over systems and catching threats before they become incidents.

faqs.question: Can I pay for just one step instead of the whole course?
faqs.answer: Yes! You can start with just one step for as little as ₦20,000. Each step has its own price, and you can add more whenever you're ready. If you're able to take the full course at once, it works out cheaper (₦180,000 instead of ₦210,000 if bought step by step) — but starting small is always an option.

faqs.question: Do I need to complete Cybersecurity Foundations first?
faqs.answer: It's not a hard requirement, but we strongly recommend it — or equivalent experience with basic networking and security concepts. This course moves quickly into real monitoring tools and assumes that foundation is already in place.

faqs.question: Can I pick any step, or do I have to go in order?
faqs.answer: We recommend going in order, since several steps build directly on the SIEM and triage skills from earlier ones. You're still free to start wherever you like — if you skip ahead, we'll let you know clearly what you might want to brush up on first.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a Step Certificate and the Full Course Certificate?
faqs.answer: Every step you complete earns its own Digitanotion Step Certificate. Once you've completed all 6 steps, you also receive the Digitanotion SOC Analyst Certificate (Tier 1), recognised by our industry partners as full Tier 1 SOC readiness.

faqs.question: What if I only finish a few steps? Do I lose anything?
faqs.answer: Not at all. You keep every Step Certificate you've earned, and you can come back and continue at any time — there's no deadline or expiry on picking up where you left off.

faqs.question: What tools will I learn to use?
faqs.answer: You'll get hands-on with a real SIEM platform for log search and alert monitoring, Wireshark for network traffic inspection, and the same dashboards and workflows used in real Security Operations Centers.

faqs.question: Are the labs real, or just simulations?
faqs.answer: A mix of both — you'll work with real tools like SIEM platforms and Wireshark, but on safe, controlled data and scenarios built specifically for learning. You get real hands-on practice without any risk to a live system.

faqs.question: What career opportunities does this lead to?
faqs.answer: Graduates are ready for entry-level roles like Tier 1 SOC Analyst, Security Monitoring Analyst, or Junior Threat Detection Analyst — and many go on to our Ethical Hacking specialization to build toward more advanced security roles.

faqs.question: How much time should I set aside each week?
faqs.answer: About 8–10 hours a week works well: a few hours for live sessions, a few for lab work, and some time for practice on your own. It's designed to fit around work, school, or family life.

faqs.question: What kind of projects will I work on?
faqs.answer: You'll work through a real-style alert triage queue, a full guided incident response walkthrough, and network traffic analysis — building the exact muscle memory a working Tier 1 Analyst uses every shift.

faqs.question: What support do I get during the course?
faqs.answer: A dedicated mentor, round-the-clock access to your practice labs, a student community, weekly office hours, and career guidance once you're done.

faqs.question: Is this course suitable for someone with zero cybersecurity background?
faqs.answer: It's best if you've covered the basics first — we recommend our Cybersecurity Foundations course if you're starting completely from zero. From there, this course takes you straight into real, practical SOC work.
